svg.title: Level 4 BCA: a funding allocation formula
svg.desc: Level 4 BCA: a funding allocation formula. Stages run across and lanes run down. A funding allocation formula, which NHSBSA's Analytical Assurance Decision Tool gives as a worked example of impact 4, which is Level 4 BCA at every likelihood. The route this playbook sets out for work of that kind, not a record of a particular piece of work. Stages, left to right: Engagement and scoping, Design, Analysis, Delivery and sign-off and Review. Commissioner. Owns the question and the resource. Engagement and scoping: State the decision, the deadline, and how certain the answer has to be. Agree the sheet with the analyst, and find what Level 4 assurance needs. Design: Approve the design before work proceeds. Analysis: Stay available. Resist changing the question late. Delivery and sign-off: Confirm it meets your need and apply its limitations. Review: The review is yours to own, with the Analysis Senior Responsible Officer. Analyst. Owns the method and the write-up. Engagement and scoping: Clarify the real question. Record the scope, the boundaries and the assumptions. Score the impact and the likelihood, and read Level 4 BCA off the sheet. Design: Choose the method, and place the work among the eight model types. Check the likelihood you scored still holds against it. Analysis: Do your own checks first. Log decisions as you go, and quantify the uncertainty. Delivery and sign-off: Write it up, with the caveats in the output itself. Review: Record the lessons where the next analyst will look. Critical friend. At Level 4 BCA, a Lead Assurer from outside the delivering team, with external review as well. Design: You are named at design, not found at delivery. Analysis: Reproduce the calculations from source. Examine the assumptions, and report what you find back. Delivery and sign-off: Sign off as Lead Assurer, which comes before the approval below. Review: What you reported back is what the next piece of work avoids. None: This lane is empty at Engagement and scoping. Analysis Senior Responsible Officer. Approves this one output as fit for its intended use. Engagement and scoping: You are named at scoping and the register entry is made then, not once the work is designed. Design: Confirm design governance has been followed before the analysis starts. Analysis: Stay aware of progress, and be available to approve at delivery. Delivery and sign-off: Review the evidence, then approve as fit for its intended use. Review: Revalidate the designation annually, and before any reuse for a new purpose. What is handed over. 1: Commissioner to Analyst, at Engagement and scoping. The decision, the deadline, and how certain the answer has to be. 2: Analyst to Critical friend, at Design. The design and plan, with the critical friend named on it. 3: Critical friend to Analyst, at Analysis. Findings, which are the analyst's to act on. 4: Analyst to Commissioner, at Delivery and sign-off. Draft results, so they are understood before sign-off. 5: Analyst to Analysis Senior Responsible Officer, at Delivery and sign-off. The assurance evidence. 6: Critical friend to Analysis Senior Responsible Officer, at Delivery and sign-off. Lead Assurer sign-off, which comes first. 7: Analysis Senior Responsible Officer to Commissioner, at Delivery and sign-off. Approved as fit for its intended use. Why this one is Level 4 BCA: One impact dimension at 4 settles it. The Finance row's level 4 is analysis that "determines, or is relied on for, major funding, investment, commissioning, resource-allocation or policy decisions", which is what a funding allocation formula is. So the work is Business Critical and the level is 4, said at scoping and before the design. Four roles, and between them seven pages of this playbook. Level 4 adds formal audit and external review, and the work finishes published with its quality assurance statement, on the register, and the designation revalidated annually. NHSBSA Producing Quality Analysis Playbook. Service design artefacts for workshop use. Seamus Sands for NHSBSA, SOW-DOC053.
